title: POC eval sprint scope - ClarityWorks
summary: POC scoping call to define success criteria, workload sizing, and shortlist open models for a 3-week evaluation sprint. Discussed latency/throughput targets, multilingual coverage, domain adaptation needs (financial documents), data security (VPC/KMS/SOC2), and benchmark plan. Agreed next steps to share prompts, model shortlist, and dedicated sizing recommendation.
action_items: Alice Martinez: Send model shortlist + benchmark spreadsheet and runbook by 2026-11-20
Ben Cho: Propose GPU pool sizing (est. instance types + prequantization config) by 2026-11-22
Priya Singh: Share 20 representative prompts and 500 anonymized documents for evaluation by 2026-11-23
Marta Ruiz: Schedule 1-hour kickoff with infra on 2026-11-24 to finalize VPC details
next_steps: Redwood to run baseline benchmark on 3 candidate open models (Falcon-40B, Llama2-13B, Mistral-Instruct) with customer's sample set
Customer to confirm SLA needs and data retention policy
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-19
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Alice Martinez (Redwood AE), Ben Cho (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (ClarityWorks Head of ML), Omar Haddad (CTO), Lena Park (ML Eng), Marcus Lee (Product)

Auto-generated summary: POC scope for an evaluation sprint to validate open models for multilingual and financial document tasks. Action items assigned.

[00:00] Alice Martinez: Okay good afternoon everyone thanks for joining, um we're excited to run through the POC scope for ClarityWorks. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Priya Singh: Hi Priya here, thanks Alice.
[00:15] Omar Haddad: Omar on the line.
[00:17] Lena Park: Lena here.
[00:20] Marcus Lee: Marcus joining as well.
[00:23] Ben Cho: Ben from Redwood, nice to meet you all.
[00:27] Alice Martinez: Great, quick agenda — align on success criteria, confirm workload sizing, pick an open-model shortlist and agree timeline. If at any point we dive deep we can park for a follow-up SE session. Sound good?
[00:40] Priya Singh: Sounds good. High level we need high accuracy on extraction and summarization for financial forms in EN/FR/DE and also plausible latency for live-assist.
[00:53] Alice Martinez: When you say live-assist latency, what's the p50/p95 targets you're thinking?
[00:58] Priya Singh: Ideally p50 <200ms for 256 token responses, p95 <600ms. If that's unrealistic we can trade some latency for cost, we just need predictable tail latency.
[01:15] Ben Cho: Quick note, constraint: those numbers are tight on hosted smaller GPUs, we might suggest dedicated capacity or a hybrid routing policy. Also context window — what's your typical request length?
[01:25] Lena Park: Most requests are 512 tokens with occasional 2k docs when we do batch summarization. So we'd like support up to 8k context but we don't need it low-latency for the big ones.
[01:36] Marcus Lee: And regionally we'll be mostly EU and NA, with some FR-specific regs. Data residency matters for FR customer subsets.
[01:45] Alice Martinez: Noted. On security — are you expecting Private deployment or hosted with VPC peering?
[01:50] Omar Haddad: We prefer VPC/private plane if possible. We have KMS for keys and need audit logs, SOC2 plus ISO27001 would be ideal.
[02:00] Marta Ruiz: We can support VPC connectors and KMS integration, and we have per-request audit logging. We'll send the security checklist.
[02:07] Priya Singh: Awesome. Back to model quality — we're evaluating open models only. Which candidates should we run initially?
[02:14] Ben Cho: For initial coverage I'd recommend three: Falcon-40B (good multilingual backbone), Llama2-13B (cheap and fast with instruction-tuning), and Mistral-Instruct (strong instruction quality on shorter context). Those give a variety of latency vs quality tradeoffs.
[02:29] Lena Park: Curious about performance on FR/DE — does Falcon do well there?
[02:34] Ben Cho: Falcon historically is okay but BLANK — sorry... sometimes falcon drops on some RTL languages. For FR/DE it usually holds up; Mistral has surprisingly solid cross-lingual transfer but might need adapters or fine-tuning for domain-specific terms.
[02:52] Priya Singh: Fine-tuning is possible but for the POC we want to avoid heavy retrain. Prefer lightweight instruction-tuning or retrieval-augmented prompts.
[03:01] Alice Martinez: Noted. Success criteria we'll propose: accuracy (F1 on extraction) > 0.88, semantic summary ROUGE-L relative > 0.7, p50 latency <250ms average for 256 tokens, throughput target 25 QPS for typical route, memory/instance within dedicated pool sizing. Does that sound reasonable?
[03:20] Omar Haddad: The accuracy thresholds are fine, throughput maybe 25 qps is optimistic — our peak is closer to 15 qps but 25 gives headroom.
[03:30] Marcus Lee: Also include error budget for hallucinations — we need a low false-positive rate on extraction.
[03:36] Ben Cho: We'll add hallucination metrics and calibration checks.
[03:40] Alice Martinez: On benchmarks — we'll run latency, p50/p95, tokens/sec, memory footprint, and quality (F1/ROUGE) across three models and two quantization configs (8-bit and 4-bit if feasible). How does that sound?
[03:54] Priya Singh: Good. For quantization, we worry about quality drop with 4-bit — we want to measure that.
[04:00] Ben Cho: Absolutely. We'll do 8-bit first, then 4-bit-llm test and run a quality delta. We'll also test KV cache behavior for long chat sessions.
[04:13] Lena Park: For chat we do long-running sessions with KV cache; any known tradeoffs there?
[04:18] Marta Ruiz: Bigger context and caching tends to increase memory linearly; for dedicated pools we can size instance types (A100 vs H100) to handle KV. We'll recommend a mix — smaller instances for quick responses, bigger ones for batch summarization.
[04:33] Marcus Lee: Which GPU types do you think for 13B vs 40B models?
[04:38] Ben Cho: Llama2-13B can do well on 1xA10 or A100-40GB with 8-bit; Falcon-40B we usually put on A100-80GB or H100 with sharding or optimized kernels. Mistral sits somewhere in between often with 2xA100-40GB depending on quantization.
[04:58] Alice Martinez: Let's talk timeline — target POC kickoff week of 2026-11-29 and run 3 weeks: week 1 baseline + data ingest, week 2 benchmarks, week 3 quality review + decision. Any blockers?
[05:12] Priya Singh: We can do that if we get the benchmark template and model shortlist this week and internal approvals for sharing sample docs.
[05:20] Omar Haddad: Legal will need the DPA before data exchange.
[05:24] Alice Martinez: We'll share DPA + security checklist with Marta.
[05:28] Marta Ruiz: I'll follow up on DPA and set up a secure upload bucket with temporary creds.
[05:33] Ben Cho: For measurement we'll provide a small harness that runs synthetic traffic and logs tokens, latency, and quality metrics; we'll publish a CSV and a small dashboard.
[05:45] Lena Park: On multilingual prompts, we will provide parallel prompts in EN/FR/DE for the same tasks so you can compute per-language deltas.
[05:55] Alice Martinez: Great — question for ClarityWorks: is there a budget constraint driving hosted vs dedicated?
[06:02] Priya Singh: We have a mid-range budget for POC. If dedicated is too expensive we can start hosted but need guarantees on egress and retention.
[06:12] Ben Cho: Hosted hybrid is possible — route low-latency traffic to hosted optimized pools and large batch to dedicated or on-demand. We can demo routing rules.
[06:24] Omar Haddad: Any compliance concerns with hosted?
[06:27] Marta Ruiz: Hosted can meet SOC2, and we provide VPC peering for isolation; for customers requiring full private control we offer the Private plane deployment (that needs longer lead time).
[06:39] Alice Martinez: What's lead time for Private?
[06:42] Marta Ruiz: Typically 6–8 weeks for Private (VPC & on-prem variants), so for POC we usually do hosted with VPC or Dedicated reserved pool.
[06:52] Priya Singh: Ok we'll aim for hosted with VPC for POC to move faster.
[06:57] Ben Cho: Back to models — any internal embargo on model families? Some legal teams prefer avoiding models with less clear licenses.
[07:05] Omar Haddad: Right want permissive licensing. We need license docs for each candidate.
[07:09] Alice Martinez: We'll include licensing notes in the model shortlist.
[07:12] Marcus Lee: About evaluation data — can you clarify anonymization level we need? We can hash IDs and remove PII fields but maintain structure.
[07:20] Priya Singh: That works; we can provide schema and anonymize. We want to keep domain tokens intact for accuracy testing.
[07:28] Ben Cho: For benchmarking we'll need a holdout test set for quality checks that we won't use for prompt tuning.
[07:35] Lena Park: We'll designate 20% of the samples as holdout.
[07:38] Alice Martinez: Good. Any concerns about model hallucinations?
[07:42] Priya Singh: Yes false positives in extraction would be high risk for us. So we'll measure precision strictly and set thresholds.
[07:50] Ben Cho: We'll include precision/recall and a hallucination score (percentage of unsupported assertions).
[07:57] Marta Ruiz: Also adding automatic regression alerts — if quality drops below threshold during quantization we'll flag it.
[08:04] Omar Haddad: Excellent. Let's capture technical acceptance criteria again: F1 >0.88 extraction, ROUGE-L >0.7 summary, p50 <250ms for 256 tokens on low-latency route, throughput ~15–25 QPS, and quantization quality delta <5% relative.
[08:22] Alice Martinez: I'll write that into the runbook.
[08:25] Marcus Lee: Anything about caching strategies?
[08:28] Ben Cho: We'll use prefix caching for repeated documents; Redwood runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching for generation reuse which should reduce token cost for repeated prompts.
[08:40] Priya Singh: Will the cost model show token-level breakdowns per route?
[08:44] Marta Ruiz: Yes cost per token + per-request overhead, and we'll show a simulator for unit economics.
[08:51] Alice Martinez: Competitors — are you evaluating anyone else in parallel?
[08:55] Omar Haddad: We have a parallel eval with an internal endpoint and are talking to a hosted vendor. No signed decision yet.
[09:02] Alice Martinez: Understood. Any other technical unknowns?
[09:05] Lena Park: One question — do you support custom quantization recipes or only standard 4-bit/8-bit?
[09:10] Ben Cho: We support standard 8-bit and multiple 4-bit pruned modes; we can also test custom kernel combos but that takes more SE time. For POC we'll do standard quant configs first.
[09:22] Priya Singh: Ok. For the benchmark harness, do you need exact GPU SKUs?
[09:27] Ben Cho: If you can give expected instance type we can try to match; otherwise we'll propose reasonable defaults.
[09:33] Alice Martinez: Recap and owners: Alice will send model shortlist + runbook; Ben will size GPU pool and provide benchmark harness; Marta will send security checklist and DPA; Priya will provide data samples and holdout. Kickoff target week of 11/29.
[09:52] Omar Haddad: Sounds good.
[09:55] Marcus Lee: A couple clarifications — can we see historical latency traces from similar customers?
[10:00] Marta Ruiz: We'll anonymize an example and share it.
[10:04] Priya Singh: Great.
[10:06] Alice Martinez: Any final questions?
[10:09] Lena Park: No, thanks.
[10:11] Alice Martinez: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials.
[10:13] Ben Cho: Thanks, bye.
[10:15] Meeting end.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., "dedikate" for dedicated) and speaker overlaps. Shared artifacts: link: https://redwood.example.com/pocs/clw/runbook (action: Alice to populate); security checklist doc link to be sent by Marta.
